mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the months when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 0.2 percentage points over a three-month period indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the past two months indicates a broad-based economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months where both HOUST and INDPRO decline by at least 0.5% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when CPIAUCSL is above 3.0% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below 560 billion dollars signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to lower corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS falls below 560,000 million dollars.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening labor market combined with monetary policy tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS declines by at least 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.10 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0), which indicates a slowdown in manufacturing, the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when INDPRO is below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals weak demand for residential construction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when HOUST declines by at least 0.5% from the prior month.
